title: Belt Squat
summary: A squat with the load hung from a hip belt, which trains the legs hard without loading your spine.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: commercial gym machine (this exercise's own machine).

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for quads (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly quads total.
Library rating 0.7 for glutes (helper): each working set adds 0.7 of a set to the weekly glutes total.
Library rating 0.6 for adductors (helper): each working set adds 0.6 of a set to the weekly adductors total.

setup.text: Stand on the platform with the belt around your hips.
Squat down between your hips, holding the rails lightly.
Go deep, then drive back up.

form_cues.cue: Keep your torso upright. Your hands are for balance, not for pulling.

mistakes.text: Letting the hips shoot back so the belt swings.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds two or three ramp-up sets at rising loads before the first working set, unless that load is very light.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 6-10 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train comfortably.

alternatives.why: Swap sheet: Less stretch emphasis, One side at a time, Lower loading potential.

notes: Ratings, swap attributes and cues are the library model (modeled). An authored page will replace this one.
